transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start time (UTC): 14:00
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), John Morales (CTO, CedarWorks), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Aaron Kim (Security), Elena Ruiz (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on OPA policy gating, packaging, KMS and telemetry; list next steps and owners.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. Liam's our SE, he'll take most of the deep dive.
00:12 John Morales: Hi all, John here. we just spun up a sandbox cluster to try the operator, wanted to make sure packaging is right for our listing process.
00:20 Priya Singh: Priya here — we'll be owning the CI gating and OPA integration. got a few questions about how the policies are expected to be authored.
00:28 Liam Patel: Awesome. high level, we recommend embedding OPA checks as a pre-merge step in your release pipeline. Redwood's reconciler exposes a small webhook we can tie into or you can run opa eval against generated manifests.
00:43 Aaron Kim: From security, we need to understand what audit logs look like — S3 format or JSON lines? also, do you require key rotation policies for KMS?
00:55 Liam Patel: Good call. our listing cert asks for structured JSON logs with time, request id, model id, and tenant id. rotation itself can be customer-managed — we support external KMS via our operator but there are a few notes about envelope encryption that I'll share.
01:18 Maya Chen: I'll drop the packaging checklist, it has the required fields for marketplace metadata, cert tests, and a sample Helm values yaml.
01:27 Priya Singh: Great. on OPA: does Redwood publish a policy library or do we author rules per-integration?
01:36 Liam Patel: We have a small set of example policies in the partner repo. most customers copy them and adapt. typical gates are: network egress rules, RBAC scoping, PV retention, and KV cache eviction settings (sorry that's K V cash in the doc sometimes).
01:55 John Morales: PV retention and eviction — can we tune those per-tenant? our infra team wants control over eviction thresholds.
02:05 Liam Patel: Yes, those are configurable via values and you can overlay with kustomize. we'll share a kustomize overlay that sets tenant-level thresholds.
02:18 Elena Ruiz: On telemetry — what minimal metrics do you need for listing acceptance? request latency buckets, token counts, and health probes?
02:29 Liam Patel: Exactly. we ask for those three plus a few counters: failed model loads, cache hits/misses, and GPU memory pressure. Prometheus format is preferred; standardized labels: instance_id, region, model_variant.
02:46 Aaron Kim: For audit logs, do you support pushing to a customer S3 or must it come to Redwood?
02:53 Maya Chen: For Private listings, customer push is preferred; for hosted it goes to our ingestion. for listing certification we need a sample export showing the fields.
03:05 Priya Singh: On the CI gating, we run OPA in our pipeline and can fail merges. would Redwood prefer policy-as-code tests be in partner repo or in our repo?
03:16 Liam Patel: Ideally both: partner repo stores canonical policy examples and your repo contains the tests and any custom rules. during certification we'll run the partner repo policies against your manifests as a smoke gate.
03:30 John Morales: Any required e2e test harness? we have a small load generator but not model-specific traffic drivers.
03:38 Liam Patel: We have a lightweight harness (partner-load) that simulates token-level traffic and exercises streaming. it's in the partner repo; we'll provide a quickstart. it verifies latency, streaming correctness, and graceful fallback behaviors.
03:54 Maya Chen: Quick note on SSO — the marketplace requires SAML metadata for listing owners and RBAC mapping for roles. Aaron, that's probably on your plate.
04:03 Aaron Kim: Yep. we use Okta. need to confirm service account mapping and group sync. also need to confirm which roles Redwood expects.
04:12 Liam Patel: We'll send a mapping doc: roles (admin, operator, viewer) and expected claims.
04:20 Priya Singh: One technical doubt: when you say external KMS, is that only for private deployments or can it be used for dedicated?
04:29 Liam Patel: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted requires Redwood-managed keys for multi-tenant compliance, though we can sign a contract for bring-your-own-key in special enterprise cases.
04:45 John Morales: Can we get a patch that demonstrates envelope encryption with Hashicorp? our stack uses HCP Vault.
04:52 Liam Patel: Yes — we'll provide a snippet. note that we recommend keeping the master key lifecycle in Vault and using the operator to reference the key via Kubernetes secrets.
05:05 Maya Chen: Alright let's talk timeline: what's the earliest CedarWorks could run the gate tests?
05:12 Priya Singh: If we get the sample policies this week we can spin up CI gates in two weeks, so end of next week for a first pass.
05:22 Maya Chen: Sounds good. we'll aim to have checklist and Helm values by 3/25. Liam will push the operator quickstart and KMS notes by 3/24.
05:30 Elena Ruiz: For telemetry, is there a minimal retention we have to promise?
05:36 Liam Patel: For listing acceptance we need 30 days of sample metrics; longterm retention negotiable.
05:44 John Morales: Competitors question — is there anything Redwood enforces that AstraServe doesn't?
05:51 Maya Chen: One difference is our unified runtime emphasis — we require the telemetry and audit shape so marketplace can do cross-listing observability; relative to NimbusAI we also have a stricter prefix cache diagnostic requirement.
06:08 Priya Singh: Could we see an example audit log file? even a redacted sample would help.
06:13 Liam Patel: Yes, sample will be included in the checklist bundle.
06:20 Aaron Kim: For the CI gate, do you support a mode where Redwood runs validations from CI against our staging cluster?
06:28 Liam Patel: We can run validations as part of the partner certification sprint — either runbooks or access via short-lived credentials. we prefer tests to run in your CI but we can offer a validation run with our infra if needed.
06:43 Maya Chen: Okay wrapping to next steps: we'll share the pack, sample policies, helm values, operator quickstart and the load harness links. set a follow-up 30–45 minute runbook session week of 3/29.
06:57 John Morales: Perfect. thanks everyone.
07:01 Priya Singh: thanks, bye.
07:04 Aaron Kim: bye.

Note: transcription contains minor mis-hears (KV cache -> K V cash). references to repos: partner repo (https://git.redwood.example/partners/cedarworks) — link placeholder.
